subject: 1980s energy model beats modern AI loops by 1,000x in speed
intro: Claude Code got custom themes and smarter project coordination this week. Fun, but almost decorative next to the real story. CRAM just showed that a 1985 physics idea outperforms modern reasoning loops by 1,000x in training speed. We keep building bigger, and a 40-year-old energy function quietly solves Sudoku in 42ms on one GPU. The pattern: the best ideas aren't always the newest ones.

news.headline: Claude Code desktop app now supports custom themes with animated backgrounds
news.body: Claude Code just got a glow-up. You can now build custom themes for the Claude Code desktop app using a feature called mods, which are small plugins that change how the app looks and behaves. Want a dark purple background with animated particles? Just describe it to Claude and it builds the theme for you. No design skills needed. Here is what you can do right now: To try it, update to the latest desktop version . Themes currently work in local sessions only. The fun part: you do not need to write a single line of CSS. Just tell Claude what vibe you want. It handles the rest. Your terminal, your aesthetic.
bullets: Change colors across the entire UI
Use the theme-examples plugin to get started fast with pre-built scenes
Write your own theme from scratch using the official docs

news.headline: Anthropic upgrades Claude Code Projects with smarter coordination and thread sharing
news.body: Claude Code just got a solid upgrade to its Projects feature, and it changes how you manage complex, multi-part work. Projects let Claude run multiple tasks at the same time in separate threads, like having several conversations going in parallel. The coordinator, the part that oversees everything, now speaks up more. It answers your questions directly in the project chat and gives you live status updates on what's running. Projects is in public beta on Pro and Max plans. Join the waitlist if you don't have access yet.
bullets: Share threads as read-only links with anyone signed into Claude
Set reminders on any thread so it hides until you need it, then Claude surfaces it automatically
/btw spins off a new thread mid-task so your current one stays focused
/fork branches a thread so you can try a different approach without losing your original
Artifact thumbnails now show inside each thread for faster navigation

news.headline: DeepSeek opens web search, file parsing, and voice to API developers
news.body: DeepSeek just gave its V4.1-Flash model a serious upgrade. The tools powering the DeepSeek consumer app are now available through the API. No more stitching together third-party services. Before this, adding web search or PDF parsing to your AI app meant calling external APIs yourself and manually assembling the context. Until now, incorporating web search, PDF parsing, or speech recognition required setting up your own infrastructure. That changes now. Here is what you can plug in with a few parameters: Enable search with deepseek_web_search and URL reading with deepseek_read_url. Tool usage is billed on top of normal token prices. Public apps must have safety checks on.
bullets: Web Search : the model searches the web and returns cited answers automatically
Deep Thinking Search: searches and reads pages during multi-step reasoning
File Input: drop in PDFs, Office files, or images and the model reads them
URL Reading: paste a link in a message and the model fetches and reads it
Safety Checks: screens inputs and outputs, flags risky content automatically
